questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
Which government policy is not aimed at correcting inefficiency in resource allocation?

options.A: marginal cost pricing in state owned industries
options.B: permits restricting the pollution of rivers by private firms
options.C: requiring firms to pay a minimum wage
options.D: the provision of public goods at zero price

questions.questionText: The table shows some of the costs and benefits, in $ millions, associated with a road building project. Both a government department and a profit-maximising private firm are considering building the road. private external external social costs costs benefits benefits 450 75 50 550 Who would be willing to build the road?

options.A: Both would be willing to build it.
options.B: Neither would be willing to build it.
options.C: Only the government department would be willing to build it.
options.D: Only the private firm would be willing to build it.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, Q is the quantity produced of a good as the result of market forces. price S (social cost) S (private cost) D O Q quantity Which concept is present at output Q ?

options.B: a negative externality
options.C: a positive externality
options.D: a specific tax

questions.questionText: What would not affect the budget line of an individual consumer?

options.A: the individual’s preference for various goods
options.B: the level of income tax
options.C: the money prices of goods
options.D: the wages earned by the individual

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for a product. D price O X quantity What is maximised at X?

options.B: total revenue
options.C: marginal utility
options.D: total utility

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. costs, revenue P MC MR D MR O Q output Which features are associated with the diagram?

options.A: economies of scale and allocative efficiency
options.B: interdependence and allocative efficiency
options.C: price rigidity and economies of scale
options.D: price rigidity and interdependence

questions.questionText: In the year ending July 2016, airline fuel prices fell by 20.4% while the price of passenger aircraft increased by around 1.1%. Assuming no other changes in the passenger airline industry, what was the outcome for fixed costs and variable costs? fixed costs variable costs

options.B: decreased increased
options.C: increased decreased
options.D: increased increased

questions.questionText: Which feature of production would make it more likely that an industry is a contestable market?

options.B: all firms in the industry share research and development
options.C: low fixed costs
options.D: market rivals aim to reduce product differentiation

questions.questionText: What is an example of backward vertical integration?

options.A: a bakery buying a wheat farm
options.B: a car manufacturer buying a car showroom
options.C: a vineyard buying an apple orchard
options.D: two rival supermarkets joining together

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm in imperfect competition. It changed its aim from profit maximising to sales revenue maximising. cost, MC revenue AC AR MR O output Which type of profit was it making in each case? profit sales revenue maximising maximising

options.B: subnormal profit normal profit
options.C: supernormal profit normal profit
options.D: supernormal profit supernormal profit

questions.questionText: An airline sells seats at $100 each three months before a flight, at $150 each one month before the flight and at $200 each the day before the flight. What describes this type of market behaviour by the firm?

options.A: limit pricing to deter entry in an imperfect market
options.B: price discrimination by a monopoly supplier
options.C: price leadership by an oligopolist
options.D: pricing where price equals average cost under perfect competition

questions.questionText: What would not be an indication of a divergence between the interests of the managers and the shareholders of a company?

options.B: management salaries which are linked to the long-run growth of the company’s share price
options.C: the acceptance of ‘X’ inefficiency in the company’s production process
options.D: the purchase of artwork for a company’s headquarters

questions.questionText: The total cost to a school of employing ten cleaners is $60 per hour. The school estimates that the hourly marginal cost of employing an eleventh cleaner would be $11.50. By how much would the hourly wage have to increase to employ an additional cleaner?
What would cause a rise in the productivity of labour?

options.B: an increase in the quality of capital
options.C: a rise in consumer surplus
options.D: a rise in the elasticity of supply of labour

questions.questionText: In the diagram D and S are the initial demand and supply curves for building workers. wage S Y Z U T X D R 2 D O V W quantity of labour If the demand for building workers increases to D by how much does the economic rent earned by building workers rise?

options.A: RUZ B TUZX C VXZW D XYZ

questions.questionText: Under which circumstances will a subsidy from the government be most beneficial if there are externalities from producing good X? externality caused price elasticity of by good X demand of good X

options.B: negative >1
options.C: positive <1
options.D: positive >1

questions.questionText: Which tax would help a government achieve a more equal distribution of income after tax?

options.A: a constant rate sales tax applicable to all goods and services
options.B: a constant rate tax per person
options.C: an income tax with a constant marginal rate over the whole income range
options.D: an income tax with a tax-free allowance and a constant marginal rate thereafter

questions.questionText: A country has a population of 100 million. There are 5 million people unemployed and the country has an unemployment rate of 10%. What is the size of the labour force?

options.A: 10 million B 50 million C 90 million D 95 million

questions.questionText: Which type of unemployment is correctly linked to the description of its cause? type of description of the cause unemployment

options.A: cyclical a change in demand due to holiday periods
options.B: frictional a lack of sufficient information
options.C: structural a temporary change in consumers’ expenditure
options.D: technological a general decrease in the demand for goods

questions.questionText: Growth rates can be calculated using changes in the value of GDP from year to year. Why is real GDP per head considered to be a better indicator than nominal GDP per head for this calculation?

options.A: Real GDP adjusts for price changes by using a base year.
options.B: Real GDP ignores the effects of fluctuations in exchange rates on purchasing power.
options.C: Real GDP includes changes in the size of the population.
options.D: Real GDP measures GDP at factor cost rather than market prices.

questions.questionText: What would not exist in a free market, open economy?

options.B: household saving
options.C: import spending
options.D: indirect taxation

What is a part of Keynesian economic analysis?

options.A: a liquidity trap below which interest rates are ineffective
options.B: an equilibrium price that always clears the market
options.C: a small value for the government expenditure multiplier
options.D: a vertical short-run aggregate supply curve

questions.questionText: What will definitely increase a country’s Gross National Product?

options.B: an increase in the marginal propensity to import
options.C: an increase in the value of a country’s currency
options.D: increased government expenditure on education

questions.questionText: According to the accelerator theory, what determines this year’s net investment?

options.B: last year’s output
options.C: the change in last year’s investment
options.D: the change in last year’s national income

questions.questionText: What is likely to follow if a central bank sets negative interest rates?

options.B: an increase in the rate of inflation
options.C: a reduction in bank lending
options.D: deflation in the economy

questions.questionText: The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) fell by 3% in a year. Unemployment was regarded as unacceptably high. Which combination of policies would a government be most likely to adopt in such circumstances?

options.A: an appreciation of the currency, together with an increase in the rate of interest
options.B: increased government expenditure on education, together with an increase in taxes to pay for it
options.C: increased indirect taxes, together with a depreciation in the exchange rate
options.D: reduced income taxes, together with a cut in the rate of interest
